newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil GDP growth seen slowing -- Ipea.
newsitem.headline: Brazil GDP growth seen slowing -- Ipea.

text.p: Brazil's gross domestic product (GDP) is forecast to grow 3.3 percent in the 12 months to the end of September 1997, slowing from a 4.7 percent growth rate in the year to the end of March, said the Institute of Applied Economic Research (Ipea).
Ipea, which reports to the Brazilian Planning Ministry, said in a statement it expects Brazil's GDP to grow 0.5 percent and 1.4 percent in the second and third quarters, respectively.
April industrial output is expected to increase 8.6 percent on March and 12.8 percent on April 1996, the statement said.

Ipea said the estimated increase in industrial production could be either the result of consumers rushing out to buy goods because they fear credit restrictions by the government, or of retailers stocking up ahead of Mother's Day on May 11.

Ipea said industrial production in the 12 months to the end of June was expected to rise 5.6 percent, up from 5.1 percent in the year to the end of March, but to increase only 3.3 percent in the 12 months to the end of September. ((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
